about.title: San Mateo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grief does not follow a schedule, and neither should the decisions that come after a sudden loss. In San Mateo, a city of roughly 103,000 people set between US-101 and the hills along SR-92, four people died in traffic collisions in 2025, according to public records. Each of those numbers was a parent, a partner, a child, or a friend. Not every death leads to a claim, but when a preventable act on S El Camino Real, a workplace, or a property owner's premises takes a life, California law allows certain family members to bring a civil action. That case is separate from any criminal charges. It can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Our team handles wrongful death claims in San Mateo County on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why San Mateo Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim, beginning with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can explain where your family fits before any decisions are made.

items.title: Attention to the two-year deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims involving a city, county, or state agency carry a much shorter window. Getting started early protects your ability to act.

items.title: A full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, the law recognizes lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so your family pays nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on US-101 near San Mateo. Can we still bring a claim if the driver is facing criminal charges?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death case is a civil action and runs on a separate track from any criminal prosecution in San Mateo County. The criminal case addresses punishment; the civil case addresses your family's losses. One does not have to finish before the other begins, and our team can explain how the two may interact.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases, the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a government entity is involved, such as a claim tied to a city-maintained road or a public vehicle, a formal claim must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Because the clock varies, it is wise to speak with an attorney well before those dates approach.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing is limited by statute. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs if there is no spouse or child. Families sometimes assume a sibling or parent can file automatically, so it helps to have an attorney review the specific relationships involved.
